newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico reducing grain imports - Ag Minister.
newsitem.headline: Mexico reducing grain imports - Ag Minister.

text.p: In the first five months of the year Mexico imported only a third of the corn and sorghum it imported in the same timeframe last year, Mexico Agriculture Minister Francisco Labastida said on Monday.
The government has estimated higher grain output for 1997 will cut Mexican imports by around 40 percent, or to five million tonnes from some 9.8 million tonnes in 1996.

"So far in the first five months of this year, in corn and sorghum we have imported a third of last year's imports," Labastida said at the opening ceremony of the National Farm Council's annual assembly.
Mexico has imported grains for the past 15 years, although import levels have fallen in recent years, he added.
Grain production in the 1997 farm cycle is expected to rise six percent to some 33 million tonnes, according to government figures. In 1996 grain output was 31.2 million tonnes.
